title: `dev` rehearses the cutover's end state but not its cutover mechanics: setDispatcher, replaceDispatcher and hook.pull() are executed zero times

description: `DeployMainnetPromotionReady.s.sol` calls `setDispatcher` 9 times, `replaceDispatcher` 9 times and `hook.pull()` at least 3 times. `DeployMocks.s.sol` calls each of them ZERO times. Verified on the live chain: `NFTMinterV2.nextIndex == 8` with `configs[1..7]` each populated exactly once and never repointed — the local chain deploys the post-cutover dispatcher set greenfield, because it has no incumbent to displace. The mainnet script documents the per-index order at `:145-156` — `hook.pull() -> hook.setDispatcher(new) -> new.setHook(hook) -> replaceDispatcher(idx, new)` — and states in its own words that the reverse order 'would put the new dispatcher live on the index while it still carried the fresh DefaultDispatchHook that ATokenDispatcherV2's constructor gave it, so mints would SUCCEED while accruing no mint debt — a silent value leak. Never do that.' The one ordering in the whole cutover whose wrong direction is SILENT rather than loud is the one the local mirror never executes. The same omission also means these mainnet claims are never exercised locally: that `replaceDispatcher` preserves `price`/`growthBasisPoints` (asserted at `:1366-1372` and `:1536`); that `NudgeRatchet._dispatch`'s `hookTypeId() == EXPECTED_HOOK_TYPE_ID` guard holds across a hook reuse; and that `NudgeRatchetMintDebtHook`'s non-default `DEFAULT_RATIO == 100` is not silently reset. Two adjacent cutover behaviours are likewise absent with no analogue: old-batch-minter retirement (`setPauser(OWNER)` + `pause()`), and the story-074 write-once BPT custody baseline / resume-leg handling — the latter structurally un-rehearsable because `DeployMocks` writes `deploymentStatus: "completed"` unconditionally and can never record `in_progress` or `failed`.
impact: A reordering regression in the mainnet cutover script — the exact defect class the mainnet script's own comment flags as a silent value leak — would pass the local rehearsal unchanged, because the local rehearsal contains none of the calls involved. The rehearsal's green result therefore carries less assurance than it appears to, which is the concealment bar. No claim is made that the mainnet ordering IS wrong; the finding is that `dev` cannot tell you either way.
attackPath: NONE. No attacker is involved in any of the five findings at this entry point; `dev` is an anvil-only script that is never broadcast. C4 requires an attack path only for High/Medium, and no finding here is graded above Low.
recommendation: Add a Phase 7.6 to `DeployMocks.s.sol` that, after the greenfield dispatcher set is live, deploys ONE replacement dispatcher and performs a genuine `hook.pull() -> hook.setDispatcher(new) -> new.setHook(hook) -> replaceDispatcher(idx, new)` on a single index, asserting (i) mint-debt conservation across the swap, (ii) `price`/`growthBasisPoints` preserved, and (iii) that a mint attempted in the intermediate window REVERTS rather than succeeding. One index is sufficient to make the ordering executable and therefore regression-testable. Separately, run `VerifyPromotionReady.s.sol` (story 075) against the local end state — it is free there, and story 075 closed via machine approval with its own declared regression gate never run.

classification.c4Definition: QA/Low — 'state handling, function incorrect as to spec'. A test/rehearsal-coverage gap in a non-deployed local script.
classification.assetImpact: None. `dev` never broadcasts (anvil, chain 31337) and holds no value. The mainnet script it fails to rehearse was not shown to be defective.
classification.functionOrAvailabilityImpact: None today. The protocol's function and availability are unchanged by a gap in a local rehearsal. What is degraded is *verification assurance*: the local green result carries less signal than it appears to.
impactChain: 1. DeployMocks.s.sol deploys the post-cutover dispatcher set greenfield (verified on-chain: NFTMinterV2.nextIndex==8, configs[1..7] populated once, never repointed).
2. Therefore setDispatcher / replaceDispatcher / hook.pull() execute 0x locally vs 9x / 9x / 3+ on DeployMainnetPromotionReady.s.sol. ABSENCE IS PROVEN.

3. The mainnet script documents `pull -> setDispatcher -> setHook -> replaceDispatcher` and warns the reverse order is SILENT ('mints would SUCCEED while accruing no mint debt - a silent value leak. Never do that.').
4. CONDITIONAL, NOT DEMONSTRATED: *if* a future edit reorders that sequence, the local rehearsal would still pass, because it contains none of the calls involved.
5. Realised harm today: reduced assurance from a passing rehearsal. No value moves, nothing is unavailable, no attacker is involved.
classification.likelihood: n/a - no attack path exists. The exposure is a latent detection gap, not an exploitable condition.
classification.assumptions: That a reordering regression could be introduced into DeployMainnetPromotionReady.s.sol in future. No such regression exists at e1db0f1.
classification.externalRequirements: A future code change to the mainnet cutover script that no one reviews by hand.
classification.attackPath: NONE. No attacker is involved in any of the five findings at this entry point; `dev` is an anvil-only script that is never broadcast. C4 requires an attack path only for High/Medium, and no finding here is graded above Low.
classification.localScriptRubric: KEEP, and this is the rubric's central case: the greenfield shortcut is admissible in itself, but it removes the one cutover mechanic whose failure mode is silent from the rehearsal entirely.
classification.lawNotes: Law 1: recall preserved - fully reported, not suppressed, and flagged as the headline defect against the requester's stated purpose (a). Not a Law-2 item (no story requires the rehearsal).
classification.whyNotMedium: Considered seriously and rejected. C4 Medium requires protocol function/availability impact OR a value leak with a stated attack path. Here the value leak belongs to a DIFFERENT artifact (the mainnet script) and was explicitly NOT reproduced - the finding proves only the absence of the calls. Grading the untested script at the severity of the bug it might one day fail to catch would (a) charge this finding for a defect nobody has shown to exist, and (b) collide head-on with the C4 known-invalid class 'speculation on future code without demonstrated root cause'. Missing test coverage is Low/QA under C4 even when what is untested is high-risk. Holding Low is not report-tidying: the finding is reported in full, at the top of the Low bucket, with its whole narrative and the mainnet script's own warning quoted.
classification.escalationTrigger: This becomes Medium-or-higher the moment someone demonstrates an actual ordering defect (or a hook/price/growthBasisPoints regression) in DeployMainnetPromotionReady.s.sol. That would be a NEW finding at the promotion-ready entry point, not a re-grade of this one. Recommend the next promotion-ready audit carry this as an explicit hypothesis to test.

rationale: Highest-impact-ceiling finding of the run, but it is a coverage gap, not a defect: no deployed code is wrong, no asset is at risk, and the finding's own `notDemonstratedByExecution` disclaims that the mainnet ordering IS wrong. The Medium test fails at its first link.
crossReference: The unconditional `deploymentStatus: "completed"` write named in the last sentence of the description is itself ledger entry 1e8cc0dc58ba (L-01, open, re-observed STILL-LIVE this run). It is cited here as the CAUSE of one sub-gap, not re-filed. Downstream must not mint a second entry for it.
notDemonstratedByExecution: The reverse-order leak was NOT reproduced on the live chain — doing so would have required deploying a fresh six-arg BalancerPoolerV2 plus hook and repointing index 4. The ABSENCE of the calls is proven; the consequence of getting the order wrong is quoted from the mainnet script's own documentation, not independently demonstrated here.
humanReviewReason: Borderline Low/Medium. Documented above under whyNotMedium; a reviewer who believes the mainnet cutover's untested silent-leak path is itself an availability risk to the imminent cutover may argue Medium. Classifier's position is Low on demonstrated impact.
